name: Palazzo dei Normanni and Cappella Palatina
blurb: Former royal palace of the Norman kings; the Cappella Palatina inside is an Arab-Norman mosaic chapel and a must-see.

name: Palermo Cathedral
blurb: Honey-coloured, Catalan-influenced cathedral where Emperor Frederick II is buried, in a porphyry sarcophagus.

name: Catacombe dei Cappuccini
blurb: Capuchin catacombs with over 8,000 mummified former residents; some are clothed skeletons, others strikingly well preserved.

name: Piazza Pretoria
blurb: Fountain square with 16 nude statues of nymphs and figures, also called the square of shame; free to walk around.

name: Pani câ Meusa – Porta Carbone
blurb: Classic Palermo street-food sandwiches from a stall near Porta Carbone; the listing rates them among the best in town.

name: Il Proverbio
blurb: Sicilian food near the station and Quattro Canti; the listing says most dishes are cheap at €4–6.

name: dal Barone
blurb: Relaxed wine bar with a good selection of wines and good cheeseboards; open evenings Monday to Saturday.

name: The Bar Brothers
blurb: Small bar for beers and cocktails, with a few seats out on the street; open Wednesday to Sunday evenings.

name: Monreale Cathedral (day trip)
blurb: Norman cathedral begun in 1174, on a hill 8 km west of Palermo with views back over the city and the sea.

name: Basilica di San Nicola
blurb: Romanesque basilica with a gold ceiling and a crypt, home to the magnificent cathedra (bishop's throne) of Bishop Elias.

name: Bari Cathedral (San Sabino)
blurb: Older than the Basilica of St Nicholas and later refitted in Baroque style; the cathedral is free to enter.

name: Castello normanno-svevo
blurb: Symbol of Bari: a 12th-century fortress that Frederick II rebuilt in the 13th century.

name: Bari Vecchia (Old Town)
blurb: Maze of narrow alleys between the two harbours, with more than 30 churches; free to wander.

name: Osteria Vini e Cucina
blurb: Old, very informal trattoria in the old town with traditional, unpretentious cooking; the simple four-course menu is about €15.

name: Venezia 40
blurb: Old-town spot for tasty panzerotti, the small fried filled pastries Bari is known for.

name: Black Lounge bar
blurb: Bar at the exit of Giardino Garibaldi, open daily until 20:00, so more an early-evening stop than a late night.

name: Castello Svevo nightlife area
blurb: The Swabian castle district of the old town is now one of the city's main nightlife areas, with bars around the castle.

name: Lungomare seafront promenade
blurb: Said to be the longest seafront promenade in Italy; a free walk along the Adriatic, good before or after the old town.

name: San Giusto Cathedral and Castle
blurb: Walk the castle ramparts for a panorama over the city, hills and sea; a Habsburg fortress built from the 15th to 17th centuries.

name: Miramare Castle
blurb: 19th-century castle on the Gulf, about 20 minutes from Piazza Oberdan on bus #6.

name: Museo Sartorio
blurb: Art collection given to the city by the Sartorio family: 19th- and 20th-century paintings, sculptures and Tiepolo sketches.

name: Piazza Unità d'Italia
blurb: Europe's largest sea-front square, lined with palaces that look like Vienna; free to wander and watch the sea.

name: Buffet da Siora Rosa
blurb: One of Trieste's oldest family restaurants, serving Triestine cooking; known for prosciutto cotto with mustard and horseradish.

name: Caffè Pasticceria Pirona
blurb: Viennese-style cake shop and café that kept its old charm; James Joyce was one of its most devoted customers.

name: The Karst (Kras)
blurb: Limestone plateau above the city, good for walking, with wide views over the Gulf and the Slovene and Croatian coasts.

name: Grotta Gigante
blurb: Huge cave that claims to be the world's biggest tourist cave; the multilingual guided tour takes about 45 minutes.

name: Parthenon
blurb: Fifth-century BC temple on the Acropolis, built in thanks for the victory over the Persians; later a church, then a mosque.

name: Acropolis Museum
blurb: Modern museum at the foot of the Acropolis; timed-entry tickets are required, so buy online in advance.

name: National Archaeological Museum
blurb: Athens' largest and most popular museum, with the Mycenae treasures and a huge sculpture collection; usually very crowded.

name: Museum of Greek Folk Art
blurb: Overlooked folk-art museum in Plaka: tools, folk pottery, primitive painting and furnished interiors; very cheap.
priceText: €2; students from non-EU countries €1; under-19s and EU students with ID free

name: Stavros Niarchos Cultural Centre
blurb: Free cultural complex in Kallithea with a terrace view of the Acropolis and the coast; good for a relaxed afternoon.

name: To Kioupi (basement taverna)
blurb: Basement taverna known as 'the hole in the ground', serving authentic, inexpensive traditional Greek food.

name: Laiki (People's market)
blurb: Working fruit, vegetable and fish market where locals shop; good fun to browse.

name: Taf (The Art Foundation)
blurb: Cultural venue and bar with strong cocktails and jazz and soul music; open until about 04:00.

name: Pame Psirri
blurb: Mezedopolio on Agii Anargiri square in Psirri, where local singers perform rebetiko over small plates.

name: Saint Demetrios (Agios Dimitrios)
blurb: Mid-7th-century basilica built over Roman baths and dedicated to St Demetrius, the city's patron saint; free to enter.

name: White Tower
blurb: The 16th-century fortified tower that became the city's symbol; later a prison, it now holds a small history museum.

name: Palace of Galerius
blurb: Ruins of the palace complex of Emperor Galerius, the Roman ruler who also built the nearby Rotunda.

name: Museum of Byzantine Culture
blurb: Museum of Early Christian and Byzantine life: churches, cities, cemeteries, castles and monasteries; the student ticket is half price.

name: Modiano Market
blurb: Traditional central food market with hundreds of stalls for meat, fish, produce, herbs and spices, plus cheap clothes.

name: Pizza Chris
blurb: Budget pizzeria with well-made dough and bold flavours; the listing calls it one of the nicest pizzas in town.

name: Mylos Club
blurb: Live-music venue hosting concerts, Greek bands and exhibitions; the listing warns the venue can change, so check their Facebook page.

name: Ouzománia
blurb: One of the oldest ouzeries in town: a small tavern with kind staff and a great atmosphere for ouzo and small plates.

name: Cultural Route bus tour (line 50)
blurb: Public bus that leaves the White Tower for a 50-minute loop past the city's main historic and cultural sights.

name: Hagia Sophia
blurb: Church completed in 537 with a 30-metre dome that was the largest enclosed space in the world for over a thousand years.

name: Topkapı Palace
blurb: Ottoman imperial palace for four centuries, with four courts, the harem and the treasury.
priceText: Combined ticket (palace, harem, Hagia Irene): foreign visitors 2750 TL; reduced 250 TL, foreign students with physical ISIC pay double (500 TL)

name: Basilica Cistern
blurb: Vast underground cistern built by Justinian in 532, with 336 columns; a cathedral-like space.

name: Santral İstanbul
blurb: Contemporary art museum in a converted 1914 coal power plant, once the oldest in Istanbul and the Ottoman Empire.

name: Ali Usta Çiğ Köfte
blurb: Cheap takeaway çiğ köfte wrap; the owner is a social-media personality, so expect a queue.

name: Kanaat Lokantası
blurb: Traditional Ottoman-style restaurant dating to 1933, famous for its desserts; reasonably priced and cash only.

name: Montreal Nevizade
blurb: One of many small bars in the Nevizade lane, with live music, beer and shots in a neon-lit setting.

name: Ağaç Ev (Tree House)
blurb: Late-night cocktail bar with live music on the Kadıköy side of the city; open until about 04:00.

name: Çemberlitaş Hamamı
blurb: Turkish bath built in 1584, credited to Mimar Sinan; a classic hamam visit in the old city.

name: Alexander Nevsky Cathedral
blurb: The largest church in the Balkans, holding around 5,000 worshippers and built to honour Russian soldiers who died.

name: National Museum of History
blurb: Bulgarian history from prehistory to today, set in a European context; over 650,000 exhibits at the Boyana residence.
when: Winter (1 Oct–31 Mar) 09:30–18:00 daily; ticket office closes 17:15

name: Sofia History Museum
blurb: History of Sofia in the colourful 1913 Central Mineral Baths, with items once owned by Bulgaria's last monarchs.

name: Petko R. Slaveykov Square
blurb: Central square with a monument to the Slaveykov writers and the Balkans' biggest open-air book market; free.

name: Boyana Church (day trip)
blurb: Small 11th-century UNESCO church on the edge of the city, with 13th-century frescoes showing early Renaissance-style realism.

name: Mekitsa and Coffee (Мекица и Кафе)
blurb: Brunch spot known for hot, fresh mekitsa, the classic Bulgarian breakfast treat; second-floor window tables are a nice seat.

name: Motto
blurb: Trendy, usually busy restaurant with modern decor; the food is consistent and many staff speak English.

name: Bar 5L
blurb: Speakeasy with designer cocktails in a cosy room; the door opens with the key that matches the day of the month.

name: 4km
blurb: Club playing mostly drum-and-bass and dubstep; entry is slightly cheaper if you arrive before midnight.
priceText: Entrance is ~€10, but slightly cheaper if you arrive before midnight

name: Palace of the Parliament
blurb: Ceaușescu's former People's House, often called the second-largest building in the world after the Pentagon.
priceText: Adults 60 lei, students 30 lei (19–26 years old, with a valid student ID)

name: Village Museum
blurb: Open-air museum of about 300 traditional buildings from across Romania, from churches to mills; founded in 1934.
priceText: Adult 15 lei; pupils and students (with valid cards) 4 lei

name: National Museum of Old Maps and Books
blurb: Small but excellent map museum over three floors; borrow a green magnifying glass to read the fine print.

name: National Art Museum
blurb: Art museum in the former Royal Palace: Romanian art from ancient to contemporary, plus rare European works from the 14th century.
priceText: 24 lei for the Romanian collection; 75% discount for pupils and students with valid cards

name: Therme București
blurb: Huge thermal water park; prices are for the Galaxy day ticket, and the higher tiers cost more.
priceText: Galaxy day ticket 141 lei Mon–Thu, 151 lei Fri–Sun and holidays; students/pupils (min. 14) 126 lei Mon–Thu, 136 lei weekends, with proof

name: Cișmigiu Garden (ice skating)
blurb: Oldest park in Bucharest, designed 1845–1860; it has ice skating in winter, with restaurants and several bars in the park.

name: Caru' cu Bere
blurb: One of Bucharest's most famous restaurants, in a historic building; a classic stop for traditional food and beer.

name: LUCA
blurb: Cheap Romanian pastry chain with branches across the city; sweet and savoury options, good for vegetarians.

name: Club A
blurb: Bucharest's oldest club, with nearly 40 years of history; an unpretentious student pub and club.

name: Kulturhaus
blurb: Club on the German culture-house model with concerts, exhibitions and film nights; the listing calls it very cheap.
priceText: Very cheap: no entry fee (listing text cut off at 'except for music')

name: Temple of Saint Sava
blurb: Serbia's largest church and one of the biggest Orthodox churches in the world, under construction since 1935; free to visit.

name: Nikola Tesla Museum
blurb: Museum on the inventor of alternating current, radio and AC motors; English guided tours are available, cash only.
priceText: English guided tour RSD800, cash only

name: Museum of Yugoslavia and Tito's Mausoleum
blurb: History of former Yugoslavia across three buildings, with Tito's mausoleum in the House of Flowers.

name: National Museum (Narodni muzej)
blurb: Founded in 1844, with more than 400,000 items over three floors from the Paleolithic to the modern era.
when: Tue, Wed, Fri, Sun 10:00–18:00; Thu, Sat 12:00–20:00

name: Znak Pitanja
blurb: Traditional Serbian restaurant; try ćevapčići with kajmak, or the offal dishes if you are feeling brave.

name: Skadarlijske kobasice
blurb: Sausage stall open daily until 03:00; the listing calls its sausages excellent.

name: Riddle Bar
blurb: Speakeasy-style cocktail bar with no fixed menu; the bartenders suggest drinks based on what you like.

name: Dogma Brewery Central
blurb: Brewery taproom with eight rotating taps, canned releases, bar food and a small courtyard.

name: Winter City Ada ice rink
blurb: Winter ice skating at Winter City Ada; other winter rinks are at Pionir Ice Hall and the Olimp sports centre.

name: Public Observatory
blurb: Four small telescopes for daytime city views; on Friday and Saturday evenings you can watch the sky with staff, if it is clear.
when: Fri and Sat night viewing from 20:30, if clear

name: Museum of Broken Relationships
blurb: Museum of objects left behind after break-ups, each with its own story; it has won a Kenneth Hudson award.
priceText: €7, 65+ & students €5.50, children under 12 free with adults

name: St. Mark's Church
blurb: Church known for its colourful tiled roof with the arms of Croatia and Zagreb; built in 1499 and free to visit.

name: Lotrščak Tower
blurb: Upper Town tower with a spiral staircase up to a lookout; the view over the city is the reason to climb.

name: Mirogoj Cemetery
blurb: Zagreb's central cemetery, opened in 1876, with picturesque arcades and a church by H. Bollé; a calm, beautiful walk.

name: Mali Medo (restaurant)
blurb: Traditional Croatian restaurant with a lively, young crowd and affordable mains; the ćevapčići and gulaš are excellent.

name: La Štruk
blurb: One of Zagreb's oldest fast-food spots; try the grilled cheese sandwich or the zagrebački sandwich.

name: KSET
blurb: Popular student club with indie and alternative programmes every night; serves only beer and soft drinks.
priceText: Entrance prices from €1.5 (students) to €6-8 for concerts

name: Jabuka
blurb: Cult club for alternative and punk music, with cheap weekend drinks and often alternative-band concerts.

name: Medvedgrad Castle and Medvednica
blurb: Mountain fortress above Zagreb with wide city views; the site has a memorial, so behave respectfully there.
priceText: Visitor Centre adults €7.95 (weekends), €6.6 (weekdays); many other ticket options
